what: HEAD-PACK (2026-10-26): the C BCIRQ8 decoder's head reads its rows from a copy of their codes and exponents packed once at load -- rows in blocks of eight, each group's segment its eight rows' exponents and then its coordinates' codes, eight bytes a coordinate -- four blocks a pass on both vector instances, every logit the rows' own bit for bit; the records of the commit that made it (27091ae against 06e67ce). In one binary the packed row dots take x0.516 of the unpacked time at the 860K decoder's head under clang (x0.401 under GCC) and x0.392 (x0.330) at TinyLlama-1.1B's head from memory, x0.599 and x0.586 (x0.448 and x0.352) at AVX2. A token of the 860K decoder takes x0.920 (clang) and x0.877 (GCC) of its time with the head packed, x0.940 and x0.855 capped at AVX2; a token of a synthetic decoder at TinyLlama's widths x0.791 (93.9 -> 73.4 ms) and x0.742. Under callgrind (the AVX2 instance) the qualification's GEM request takes 147.2 M -> 135.6 M instructions. Every generation's tokens and final logits are the unpacked head's bytes.
